changes.original: | APP-LOCAL-008 | LOCAL | Run with no arguments, the installer clones the latest release alone, without its history and with its files as the repository holds them, into ./safety.viz, installs what the release's lock file names, and starts the release's own demo script with the Node that ran the installer, ending as the demo ends; `--ref` names another release, `--dir` another directory, and `--port` and `--no-open` reach the demo. Run again where a checkout already is, it uses it as it is: nothing is cloned, and nothing is installed unless an earlier install did not finish. Run again with the `--ref` it was installed with, it does the same: the release named is the one installed when it is the tag of the installed version, `v` and that version, or the branch the clone's own git record names, and nothing is asked of the network to tell. A checkout is never moved to another release: `--ref` naming any other release where one already is stops the installer, which says to name another directory and changes nothing. A release's tag named over a clone of a branch other than `main` stops it too and names the branch, because such a branch holds a version both before and after its tag. A release that does not exist stops it with git's own reason and leaves no clone behind, and a release from before the demo command says so before anything is installed for it. Stopping the installer stops the demo it started. | safety.viz scripts/install-demo.mjs::parseInstallArgs, steps, isInstalled, holdsRelease, branchIn, spawnable | unit | tests/unit/local-demo/install-demo.test.js | ai-reviewed | OK for human review. | Each case is tested by running the file itself on a made-up release, a small git repository with nothing to install, so no test installs from the network; the run against the real repository, from an empty directory to the page answering, is recorded on the pull request (#214). `main` is the release branch, so it is the latest release. The independent review (#214) found the first version ignored `--ref` once a clone existed, reinstalled on every run, and left the demo running when the installer alone was stopped; each now has a test that failed when the fix was taken out. On Windows npm is started through a shell, as one string of its own fixed arguments; that path is tested as a function and has not been run on Windows. |
